newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -FTSE puts sold for premium as shares soar.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -FTSE puts sold for premium as shares soar.

text.p: A surge in the UK stock market on Wednesday prompted the selling of FTSE put options for premium in the belief the market will not suffer a setback, dealers said.
One large deal was to sell 3,000 August 4700 puts at 28p and through the same broker a further 4,000 lots in the same series were sold at prices of 25p and 26p.
At expiry if the market stays above 4700 the premiums collected will be the maximum profit from deals.
Other major deals were volatility trades -- in which an options position is hedged by an opposite one in FTSE futures.

The biggest of these was a put spread sold along with futures. The spread consisted of selling 1,000 August 4750 puts in FTSE at 37-1/2p and buying 1,000 August 4450 puts at 7p for a net debit of 30-1/2p. This was hedged by selling September futures at 4950.
The deal will make money if market volatility decreases.
On the bear tack, there was a buyer of 1,500 August 4400 puts at 5p which will make a profit if the market plunges.
By 1230 GMT, cash FTSE was up 67.0 to 4913.7 while September futures were up 58 points to 4936.
Over in stock options trading activity was moderate.
One of the larger deals was in British Petroleum where 487 October 700 puts were bought for 3-1/2p.
In contrast, for electronic goods retailer Dixons Group the main trade was the sale of 400 September 500 puts at 6p. A further 200 lots in the same series were subsequently sold.

And a bullish deal was struck in British Airways in which 300 October 650 calls at 24p. The shares added 6-1/2p to 634-1/2p while BP gained 16-1/2p to 826-1/2p and Dixons were 7-1/2p to the good at 552-1/2p.
